articles.title: Whence The Weeping - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Whence The Weeping is one of the first side quests you will come across in Phantom Blade Zero. It is unlocked almost right away after completing the intro and
articles.body:
Whence The Weeping is one of the first side quests you will come across in Phantom Blade Zero. It is unlocked almost right away after completing the intro and all you have to do is walk next to the man trapped in the contraption at the very beginning of the Weeping Creek Valley.

Starting it is entirely unmissable and Soul will comment on weeping he can here in the distance.

Here are the steps to complete the quest:

Continue forward on the main path until you find Yu'er. Here you will have a brief conversation about how she is looking to help her father.

At the end of this conversation, you can ask her about the Woman's Weeping.

She will mention that she can't hear it, leaving Soul to assume that only he can.

From there, you want to progress all the way through the Weeping Creek Valley until you complete Against The Flow and defeat The Hunt .

You will then enter the second region, the Crimson Forest.

Progress through the Crimson Forest until you reach the mid section of the initial path north where the objective will update and ask you to search the depths of the forest.

By following the main story, this quest will naturally progress, suggesting the weeping comes from The Chord. Now, you have to progress to the third main area: Village of Lu.

Upon entering the Village of Lu, progress forwards until you meet Jewel. This cutscene plays automatically, but when it finishes, you can ask "About the Faint Weeping". Doing so will reveal more story information and suggest The Chord is hiding in the northern mountains.

articles.summary: Super Cuccos is a Mini-Game found in Lon Lon Ranch in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to pick three super cuccos out
articles.body:
Super Cuccos is a Mini-Game found in Lon Lon Ranch in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to pick three super cuccos out of a room full of cuccos within a set time limit.

Check out IGN's full guide to Super Cuccos below.

The Super Cucco game is found in the house at Lon Lon Ranch, during the day. Speak to Talon is asleep amid the pile of chickens, speak to him to take on the challenge.

To win, find all three of his "Super Cuccos" amid the gaggle of other Cuccos in the room. The trick to finding them is to pay close attention to the mannerisms of the Super Cuccos. Compared to the regular ones, they are stiff and upright, wings angled down, and holding their heads high and flapping dramatically on occasion.

Win, and you'll get yourself a second Empty Bottle, filled with Lon Lon Milk by default.

articles.summary: Fishing Pond is a Mini-Game found in Lake Hylia in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to catch a big fish using a special
articles.body:
Fishing Pond is a Mini-Game found in Lake Hylia in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to catch a big fish using a special item, the Fishing Rod.

Check out IGN's full guide to Fishing Pond below.

Fishing Pond is a fishing mini-game in Lake Hylia. This mini-game is accessible as both Young and Adult Link. Pay 30 Rupees to start a session, then head to the water to begin. Take a second to look closely at the water and see where the biggest fish available is located.

Press ZR to aim and cast your line. Press ZR to slowly reel in, until a fish latches onto your bait. Press ZR to hook the fish, then the battle begins. You need to tilt the stick in the direction the fish is moving to wear it out. Hold ZR the whole time so that when the fish becomes tired you start reeling it in instantly.

As Young Link, catch anything over 40cm to win a Piece of Heart.

As Adult Link, catch anything over 60cm to win the Gold Scale.

You can also challenge yourself to catch the Hyrule Loach, see our detailed guide here .

articles.body:
Dampe Race is a Mini-Game found in the Lost Woods in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to follow Dampe through a twisty underground maze without losing your way.

Check out IGN's full guide to Dampe Race below.

Dampe Race is a mini-game found in the Kakariko Village Graveyard, as Adult Link only. Pull on the leftmost gravestone on the north side of the Graveyard to unveil the entrance to Dampe’s grave.

Once inside, speak to Dampe to start the race. To win, you need to follow Dampe to the end of the ruins. Fall too far behind, and you will lose automatically. You need to navigate a few obstacles along the way, and also avoid the purple flames Dampe throws behind him. Win the Dampe race once to receive the Hookshot. Return and do it again (under a minute) and you will win a Piece of Heart.

articles.title: Dandori Academy - Pikmin 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: As established in the original Pikmin 4, "Dandori" is a term describing the art of efficiency -- of commanding and directing your Pikmin to the
articles.body:
As established in the original Pikmin 4, "Dandori" is a term describing the art of efficiency -- of commanding and directing your Pikmin to the utmost level of effectiveness. Explorers in the Pikmin universe are proud of their abilities and occasionally want to put them to the test in a competitive manner.

That's the background for Dandori Academy. Imagine it like an upgraded and expanded version of the Dandori Challenges found in the game, but with a twist.

There are 72 different stages included in this new Academy mode, but they're rollout over time to create a live service game experience.

Select Dandori Academy from the Main Menu of the Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition to start. You will be welcomed by the Sage Leaf, who will test players' skills in the art and craft of Dandori.

You then create a Student ID by either reusing your main Story character or customizing and then naming your character. The Student ID acts as a stamp card that shows the medals you collect in battle.

Pikmin 4 now features voice control. You can use your voice to control Oatchi with a number of commands. The feature is off by default and needs to be enabled from the Options/Settings menu.

The "Come Back" command can be very helpful in that you call just Oatchi back out of a group of Pikmin, which is helpful if you want to have him charge and stun enemies or help to destroy objects faster without disrupting the Pikmin's work.

You can play Dandori Academy anytime after completing the first three Training levels -- but there is a catch!

Dandori Academy functions as a weekly challenge mode with Exams usually* taking place over the course of a three day period that includes the weekend across all worldwide territories.

New stages are distributed on the first Monday of each month. There are a total of 12 exam periods, with six courses each.

Players can practice them any day of the week to try and achieve the highest score and medal, but on weekends, the Exam option unlocks.

When taking an exam, you gain the ability to earn Dandori points and medals and enter a leaderboard that measures your performance against other competing players. If you miss a challenge, don't worry, you can retake previous exams during the exam period. Once you've taken an exam, you can only retry it if you have a Redo Pass. These special tickets can be earned by playing the Practice mode. You can hold up to six passes.

Dandori points unlock in-game rewards, such as status displays, Pikmin Bloom gifts, icons, stamps, and frames. The game features a built-in Reward List that tells you what point levels will unlock what.

Before playing any stage, first read through the briefing on the course screen. Apart from the overall goal and the difficulty level, you will get an important hint and details about what Pikmin are present.

The most important fact, though, is Oatchi's strength for the stage, listed in the lower left corner as Pup Strength. Oatchi's strength varies between 5, 10, 30, and 100. This corresponds to the item number designations. If Oatchi's strength is 100, he can swallow and return an item with 100 weight score -- so he's got the power of 100 regular Pikmin.

Oatchi is a crucial element when trying to get the fastest times. Not only can your character and Pikmin ride him and jump over obstacles, you can assign Oatchi to retrieve items by himself. Don't just have him follow you around while you toss and charge your Pikmin at objectives. Always assign Oatchi a task!

Pull Pikmin out of the ground. Just send him to a circle of buried Pikmin and he'll save you the time of pulling them out.

Smash through pots and fungi. Hit and hold the charge command, then let Oatchi clear the path for your Pikmin.

Stun enemies. Have Oatchi attack first, then send in your little warriors.

Pull and push obstacles according to his Pup Strength.

Don't let Oatchi idle! He's your biggest asset.

Read the objectives carefully. Some missions require you to bring everything back that you can carry, but there are many challenges that have more specific goals. For example, you may only be required to collect all treasures and gold nuggets. In that case, don't waste your time on battling -- let alone carrying -- enemies.

Create a Path and Clear Things As You Go

You might not have to defeat all enemies, but do clear out enemies that are in the path of your returning Pikmin. The same goes for stage hazards, such as flame jets, fungi, or blockers such as gates, pots, and the like.

Split up your forces to work on multiple objectives at the same time. For example, have some Pikmin and/or Oatchi open up pathways while having other Pikmin carry back objects as you wait for the path to be open.

Some stages let you build up your army by smashing objects or pulling new Pikmin out of the ground. Don't go chasing them all down first. Grow your force as you venture farther from your base. Use the Practice mode to learn about stage layout -- some courses allow you to move your base, letting you clear out one side and then moving on to another.

You will encounter small objects, heavy objects, and stashes of gold. Sometimes it's better to have a single Pikmin dedicated to a pile of gold while you clear out the rest of the stage, instead of having to run back and forth to retrieve a large number of idling Pikmin that finished a job.

If you keep all Pikmin in a perpetual leaf state, you'll fall behind with each new item you pick up and carry. Use Practice mode to find spots where you get yellow Nectar that can be used to upgrade your Pikmin.

Use Everything You've Learned in Story Mode

But remember your medal and points depend on your quick completion times. Dandori Academy is about perfecting your runs. Think about speed with everything you do. Don't toss Pikmin unless you're trying to break or stomp on things -- instead, send them in fast with X to perform a charge.

But be judicious and don't overcommit your forces to single objects. The speed gains aren't that great. It's better to split up your forces and go after many things at the same time. This also ensures that you don't have to run back to base for large numbers of idle Pikmin.

Finally, remember your Pikmin's strengths and weaknesses. Elemental abilities and resilience aside, you want to make sure you bring the right Pikmin for the job. Don't have a Purple Pikmin carry a light object, but do use Rock Pikmin to stun enemies, Red Pikmin for battling, and so on.

* At launch, the exam period was extended to last from 11/12/26 to 11/15/26, so one extra day.

articles.title: Is VisionQuest's Spoiler Character the Key to Doctor Doom's Plan in Avengers: Doomsday?
articles.summary: Is VisionQuest's spoiler character the key to Doctor Doom's plan in Avengers: Doomsday?
articles.body:
If you were wondering why you heard the sound of a million voices crying out in elation the other night, that was all the Scarlet Witch fans realizing that she was indeed coming home. Yes, as of the post-credits scene in the VisionQuest finale (which was not included in the advance press screeners, to many a writer’s chagrin) Elizabeth Olsen’s Wanda Maximoff is alive and well in the MCU. While I imagine few truly believed she was dead for good after seemingly sacrificing herself at the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, it’s been four years with nary a word about her fate from anyone at Marvel Studios. Many fans were worried she would sit out the two-part Multiverse Saga finale in Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars, but now we know that’s not the case.

The VisionQuest scene plays back the last few moments of Wanda’s fate as depicted in the Doctor Strange sequel, only to then show Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doctor Doom lifting the remains of Mount Wundagore off of her and saying “Scarlet Witch. Awaken. Your power will be mine.” For fans of the character in the MCU, it’s a huge moment. But for fans of the comics, it hints at something I’ve theorized for a long time: that Doomsday will take inspiration from Avengers: The Children’s Crusade, where Doom and Wanda have an interesting relationship. Let’s look at how Doomsday may be adapting this famous comic storyline.

Avengers: The Children’s Crusade Explained

If you’re not familiar with the source material, we’ve got you covered. Children’s Crusade was a 2010 miniseries from writer Allan Heinberg and artist Jim Cheung. It was a follow-up to Wanda’s disappearance five years earlier after the events of Avengers Disassembled and House of M. The short version is that Scarlet Witch experiences a psychotic break after being reminded of the loss of her children Billy and Tommy. She turns to the dark side, battles the Avengers, and uses her reality warping powers to create a parallel universe where mutants rule over humans under the leadership of Magneto. The dissolution of this reality and Wanda realizing what’s happened is what leads to the famous panel where she declares “no more mutants,” which started the long-running events of the Decimation story in the X-Men books.

Wanda was assumed dead after House of M, which ended in 2005. Although she made cameos in flashbacks or as doppelgängers (Loki even magically disguised himself as Scarlet Witch to infiltrate the Avengers), the real Wanda didn’t return to the mainline comic universe until Children’s Crusade in 2010. In this story, Wanda is revealed to be living in Doctor Doom’s country of Latveria. Wanda’s sons Billy and Tommy (also known by their superhero names Wiccan and Speed) go to Latveria to rescue Wanda after discovering a Doombot created to resemble her, only to learn that the real Wanda is happily engaged to Doctor Doom but without her memories of her life as an Avenger. The reveal of Wanda’s survival sends shockwaves through the superhero community, with the Avengers, Young Avengers, and X-Men all descending on Latveria at once.

Some superhero battle and time travel antics later, the heroes learn Doom was using Wanda’s powers to gain access to the Life Force, a well of mystic power related to Wanda’s innate talent of chaos magic. When Doom is imbued with the Life Force, his face is healed and the typical green tunic over his armor turns white, a precursor to his appearance in the 2015 Secret Wars comic where he becomes God Emperor Doom. With her memories restored, Wanda helps the heroes strip Doom of the Life Force and ends their relationship, but it’s left to interpretation if Doom actually cared for her or not. He claims responsibility for her actions during Disassembled and House of M by saying he manipulated her, salvaging her reputation with her teammates, but this isn’t entirely accurate, because House of M already showed that it was her brother Quicksilver who manipulated Wanda into creating that reality.

How Doomsday May Be Adapting Children’s Crusade

If you’ve been following Wanda’s story in the MCU, you may see that they’ve already set up an adaptation of Children’s Crusade. WandaVision involved her creating a pocket reality where her family was the center of the universe (albeit filtered through sitcom domesticity instead of mutant supremacy), and Multiverse of Madness featured Wanda going berserk after losing her sons and seemingly perishing. Wanda has been out of the game for a while, only to be revived by Doctor Doom at the end of VisionQuest. All of these point to Wanda being on Doom’s side during Doomsday, perhaps as part of a team with the Hulk and other heroes Doom has collected. Now that we know she’s returning, Wanda will almost certainly be a member of the Latverian witches who have been present in the marketing.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

Does Doom want Wanda’s power to help him deal with the threat of the Incursions? Or is she the conduit through which he will channel cosmic energy to become God Emperor Doom in Secret Wars? We don’t know if Doom will wipe Wanda’s memories and try to marry her like in the comics, but it’s seeming more likely that Billy (Joe Locke) and Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) will factor into the story. Given how many members of the Young Avengers have been introduced in the MCU, it’d be pretty shocking not to see the team come together in some capacity during the Multiverse Saga. But knowing how packed the Doomsday cast already is, my current theory is that the Young Avengers characters will survive Doom’s rewriting of the multiverse, leading into Secret Wars via a Life Raft.

If you’re wondering what that is, the Secret Wars comic storyline featured Reed Richards and a small handful of heroes escaping the collapse of the multiverse on a Life Raft — a vehicle capable of existing outside of time and space. This allowed the characters inside to retain their memories of the original universe instead of the new memories God Emperor Doom gave them when he assumed control of all reality. This concept will likely factor into Secret Wars, but perhaps Reed brings the Young Avengers characters, including Wanda’s sons, into the Life Raft with him, and their quest will be to restore Wanda’s memories so she can help them defeat Doom. We’ll see what happens when Doomsday drops in December, but after the VisionQuest scene, I’d be shocked if Wanda wasn’t a major part of Doom’s plans in the MCU.

How do you think Scarlet Witch will factor into Doomsday? Let us know in the comments!

Carlos Morales has been writing about sci-fi and comic book movies since 2019, and has read 10,000 comics. You can follow his fixations on Twitter .

articles.title: Elon Musk Says It 'Would Be an Honor' to Hire Jensen Huang, as the Nvidia CEO's Future Hangs in the Balance
articles.summary: Tech billionaire Elon Musk has said it “would be an honor” to hire Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, who is currently under investigation from his own board of directors and the FBI after admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy.
articles.body:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk has said it “would be an honor” to hire Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, who is currently under investigation from his own board of directors and the FBI after admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy.

The board of Nvidia is reportedly considering whether to oust its CEO . Stocks in the company have fallen on the news, and the New York Times has reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company.

The prospect of the 63-year-old Huang losing his job at Nvidia, which he co-founded in 1993, has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Nvidia provides advanced computer chips for everything from video games to cloud servers, but in recent years it has focused on the AI industry. Off the back of the enormous demand for memory to power data centers, Nvidia has become the world’s second-most valuable company, worth more than $4 trillion.

Nvidia’s board may decide to keep Jensen Huang on. Certainly tech executives have been calling for such a decision. Tim Sweeney, boss of Fortnite developer Epic Games, has been vocal in his support for Huang. He tweeted : “This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America.

“The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”

It’s worth noting that Sweeney is all-in on AI , and recently triggered a “huge pivot” of his company to retool it for “maximum AI acceleration.”

The board may, however, dismiss Huang and appoint a successor on an interim basis. Or, Huang resigns, putting himself on the market as a potential competitor to the company he built. In that scenario, Elon Musk may make a move. The Tesla owner took to his own social media platform, X , to say it would be "an honour" to work with Huang at SpaceX.

While Huang clearly has the backing of his fellow leaders in tech, he faces calls to resign from several U.S. lawmakers. There is also a reported move to tighten Nvidia China exports. Beijing has warned the U.S. not to use the spying allegations as a pretext to once again restrict tech sales to China.

Photographer: Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia Boss Amid 'Honeytrap' Scandal, Interim CEO Appointed
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993. An interim boss has been appointed by Nvidia’s board of directors.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he co-founded in 1993. An interim boss has been appointed by Nvidia’s board of directors.

Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, is appointed Interim CEO, Nvidia said. Harvey C. Jones was appointed its first-ever Chair of the Board.

In a statement, Nvidia's Board of Directors confirmed that Huang had resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. The Board said the search was on for a permanent CEO and "will consider internal and external candidates."

Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 and has been its Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since then. She leads the gargantuan company's finance organization. Before Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft.

“Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the Nvidia Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”

“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress commented. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”

Why has Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO?

Nvidia's Board of Directors and the FBI launched an investigation into the 63-year-old Huang after he admitting having an affair with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy. The New York Times then reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company. Stocks in the company fell on the news.

Nvidia provides advanced computer chips for everything from video games to cloud servers, but in recent years it has focused on the AI industry. Off the back of the enormous demand for memory to power data centers, Nvidia has become the world’s second-most valuable company, worth more than $4 trillion.

The prospect of Huang losing his job at Nvidia sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Tim Sweeney, boss of Fortnite developer Epic Games, was vocal in his support for Huang. He tweeted : “This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America. The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”

Reacting to the news of Huang's exit today, Sweeney tweeted : "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction."

Nvidia released the standard exit statement on Huang's departure, saying his controbutions to the company were "profound."

"Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world," the statement continued. "The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

Nvidia will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, and all eyes will be on the company for news of a plan for the future.

Meanwhile, Huang is now potentially on the market as a competitor to the company he built. Yesterday, SpaceX, Telsa, and X owner Elon Musk tweeted to say it would be "an honour" to work with Huang .

Whatever Huang decides to do next, his days of showing off Nvidia graphics cards live on-stage during flashy presentations are over.

articles.title: Popeyes Is Riding the GTA 6 Hype With a New 'Spice City' Chicken Sandwich
articles.summary: Popeyes has unveiled its new "Spice City" chicken sandwich, which is the restaurant's attempt to ride the hype wave for GTA 6.
articles.body:
Popeyes has unveiled its new "Spice City" chicken sandwich, which is the restaurant's attempt to ride the hype wave for GTA 6 .

Popeyes has confirmed that the Spice City chicken sandwich will be available in participating stores on November 19, the same day as Rockstar's highly anticipated release. The fast food chain said this new menu item is meant to "pay homage" to a sandwich in-game (it's unclear what in-game sandwich they are referring to, but there are drive-thrus and restaurants in GTA 6).

The sandwich includes two crispy chicken breast fillets stacked between a buttery, toasted brioche bun, topped with pickles and your choice of spicy or regular mayo. It'll set you back $6 (prices vary by location) and will be available from November 19 through November 22.

A big part of this news is that the sandwich will be available for delivery through the Popeyes app and other food delivery services, so you don't have to leave your house or worry about cooking when GTA 6 releases.

"It’s been reported that a lot of fans will be calling in sick and are clearing their calendars to disappear into the sunniest, most chaotic open world in gaming," reads a Popeyes press release. "Popeyes has the perfect getaway meal and we wanted to let you know now so you can plan ahead."

It's just one of many ways the entire world seems to be getting on board with GTA 6. In addition to a wide-ranging marketing campaign from Rockstar itself , other companies have been attaching themselves to the hype train in unofficial ways. Logitech announced that it will be giving employees the day off for video game releases going forward and will be hosting a special live-streamed event on November 19 to celebrate this perk.

Spectrum and Xfinity are also offering free internet upgrades to allow customers the chance to download GTA 6 faster. It's clear that this has become a major, global event, and companies seem to be helping advertise GTA 6 at no cost to Rockstar. Xbox and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game in both of their respective histories , highlighting the extreme hype for the title. Those who have pre-ordered GTA 6 can pre-load the game now, and they will likely want to because the game is massive.

Rockstar also confirmed that GTA 6 will run at 30fps , but will have a few enhancements for PS5 Pro users. The news came as a bit of a disappointment for some fans who were hoping for a higher frame rate, but there is hope that maybe a potential PC or PS6 port could unlock better performance later down the line.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView is my new favorite smart display — but not my daughter’s
articles.summary: Apple’s first smart display is the best smart home controller I’ve tested. But its iPhone-powered personal features let my family see each other’s texts.
articles.body: The HomeView nails everything I want from a smart display. It’s superb at controlling my smart home; it’s an excellent hands-free kitchen companion, a good speaker, and a gorgeous digital photo frame. It’s also the first Apple smart speaker with Siri AI, which is an improvement, if still slow at times. But Apple has fallen into the trap that hampers other smart displays I’ve tested: not content with doing its core functions well, it tries to do more, and that’s where the friction creeps in. --- Got questions? Ask away. We’re hosting a subscriber-exclusive AMA all about Apple’s HomeView today at 2PM ET. Drop questions here! --- The special Apple sauce here is that HomeView is both a smart display everyone in your home can use and an extension of your iPhone or iPad, providing access to your texts, calendar, and reminders when your phone is at home and on the same Wi-Fi network. This makes it a communal device with personal data, and switching between the two is where HomeView stumbles. Clunky authentication checks and being sent to my iPhone too many times interrupt the hands-free experience. Not to mention that I could easily read my 15-year-old daughter’s text messages, and vice versa. Her verdict? “I’ll just use my iPhone.” But my largely tech-averse husband fell in love with HomeView, and immediately asked for one for his office. [Product: Apple HomeView | For households deep in the Apple ecosystem, especially those with younger kids who only need access to lights and music and aren’t interested in your text messages, this may be the first smart display your whole family will actually use. But for some, the idea of their texts appearing on a large screen in the middle of the kitchen will send them running. Apple is late to the game here. Amazon and Google have had smart displays for close to a decade. But the company has debuted with a product that elevates the category in nearly every way — with a few quirks. [Image: [Image: Polished and surprisingly small The HomeView is much smaller than I expected, but it’s a great size for my needs. The star of the device is a 7-inch square touchscreen that displays a gorgeous collection of “faces” that I can customize to fit wherever I put it — the kitchen counter, bedside table, or the wall. It comes in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, and both cost $299, making it Apple’s least expensive screened device after the Apple Watch SE. The tabletop HomeView fits neatly on my kitchen counter and is light enough to move around for cooking, or when my husband wants to check his schedule over breakfast. The long USB-C cable allows plenty of maneuverability, though after a few days of spinning, it did get a bit twisty. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The screen is clear and bright and looks good in most lighting situations. It’s large enough for reading messages, following a recipe, and video calling while in the kitchen. It’s super responsive, too, showing no lag or stuttering. There’s also a Center Stage camera above the display for taking a FaceTime call while moving around, staying in frame in every corner of my small kitchen. Callers could hear me clearly, although the farther away I was, the more tinny it started to sound. Sound is very good for the size, with speakers on both the display and in the base of the tabletop model. It’s close to a HomePod Mini 2, not as room-filling, but with a touch more bass. Playing music on the wall-mounted model wasn’t as much of a downgrade as I expected in a device with one less speaker; it was richer and cleaner than on the Echo Show 15 wall-mounted in the same entryway. Siri responded well to voice commands using the device’s microphones, and as long as I remembered to put my phone face down if it was nearby, Siri replied from the correct device. [Image: The HomeView is a great music player, giving you on-screen controls, but there are no physical volume or mute buttons. The one hardware miss is physical buttons: there aren’t any. When I want to adjust the volume quickly or mute Siri, I have to tap the display or pull out my phone. I have a good spot on my kitchen counter for HomeView, but if you don’t, wall mounting is an option. Apple sent me two mounts for this review, both from Schneider Electric: a USB-C wall mount ($59.99) with a 2-meter / 6.5-foot cable and neat cable management, and a hardwired AC mount ($79.99). There will also be a power-over-Ethernet option for $129.99. The USB-C mount is easy to install: just two screws in the wall, then the display snaps on with magnets so strong that no one will accidentally knock it off the wall. [Image: [Image: However, the wall-mounted HomeView ends up costing more than the tabletop version because it’s priced the same but doesn’t include a mount or a power adaptor. You have to buy those separately, and with Apple’s $39 brick, you’re starting at around $400 (until the inevitable third-party options arrive). That’s an extra $100 for a device with fewer speakers. It’s a weird move; Apple should have included a wall mount and adapter or dropped the price. Superb in the smart home [Image: I put the wall-mounted version in my entryway, and it made it easy to control all the lights in my downstairs rooms. HomeView nails the smart display essentials: controlling my smart home, monitoring my video doorbell, providing hands-free help in the kitchen, playing music and podcasts, and displaying photos. Apple put a Thread radio and Matter controller in the HomeView, so it acts as an Apple Home hub, the first with an always-on screen. The Home app is infused throughout the device’s software, giving you multiple ways to control connected smart lights, thermostats, locks, and cameras. This is where HomeView shines. It can connect to any HomeKit or compatible Matter smart device, and it’s impressively fast at controlling them, turning on the lights in my entryway as quickly as a regular light switch. It also offers tons of options for customizing its controls. [Image: [Image: [Image: I set up the device’s Smart Home face with a large button to turn the lights on and off in the hallway it was in, plus smaller buttons for my Goodnight and Good Morning scenes, along with a live view of the Aqara video doorbell, and controls for my front door lock and Nest thermostat. In the morning, as I walk past, I hit the Good Morning scene and the house wakes up; then I do the reverse at night. Even better, my husband, who has never once opened the Home app, now turns on the lights from the HomeView every morning. The Camera face, which streams up to nine HomeKit Secure Video cameras at once, is also very fast, and when someone rings the video doorbell, HomeView pulls up a live feed instantly. I can then unlock the door right from the display. I love that I can add multiple Smart Home and Camera faces in different configurations, giving me swipeable access to all the controls I want. [Image: The Safari-based guided cooking interface is simple and intuitive to use. Smart home is my favorite use case, but I also loved cooking with HomeView. You can pull up a recipe on your phone and, using Handoff, send it to the HomeView, which brings up a guided cooking experience. This feature elicited several “Wow, that’s really cool” reactions from visitors (and my editor!). It was easy to follow the on-screen steps while cooking, as well as use Siri AI for help. While viewing a Creamy Tuscan Chicken recipe, I tapped the cherry tomatoes and said, “Siri, what can I substitute for this?” It suggested some useful options and some not-so-good ones (cucumbers?). I also liked how the HomeView automatically inserted timers into steps like “Cook the chicken for about 8 minutes on each side.” Tapping the timers popped them up into Live Activities at the top of the screen, making it easy to switch back and forth between them and the recipe. [Image: The tabletop HomeView has microphones for Siri, two drivers in the display, and a down-firing woofer and two passive radiators in the base. This switching with Live Activities also works for phone calls and music, two things I used HomeView for a lot. Answering a call on the large display while cooking is much easier than reaching for my iPhone, and the audio is loud and clear, so I could keep cooking while chatting from anywhere in the room. Music and audio playback are great; it’s nice to see album art while blasting Taylor Swift, and the screen makes it easy to pause, skip, or navigate to a new song, album, or playlist. The built-in speaker is good, but I prefer to AirPlay to compatible speakers, and I like that the HomeView remembers which I used last so I don’t have to select them each time. There are some disappointments. The HomeView has a built-in temperature and humidity sensor, like its HomePod siblings, but it can’t use its onboard 12MP camera as a motion sensor to trigger an automation. HomeView can also only control devices compatible with Apple Home, so that means no Ring doorbells or Nest cameras (without workarounds), or categories like lawnmowers or appliances that Apple Home doesn’t support. I also couldn’t get it to run some of the Siri shortcuts I use to have the voice assistant control unsupported devices. When I say “Hey Siri, feed Smokey” to any of my HomePods, they can trigger my Aqara pet feeder, but HomeView told me it couldn’t do that. Apple Home still isn’t powerful enough for advanced home setups with complicated automations or a robust home energy management system; if that’s you, you’re probably already using Home Assistant or Homey and could bring your setup into a HomeView. Which you may want to do, because HomeView’s simple, intuitive interface is great for everyone else in your home. For example, my long-suffering spouse, who just wants a way to turn on the smart lights or adjust the thermostat without pulling out his phone, asking a smart speaker, or having me do it for him. A little too personal [Image: I put the HomeView on our kitchen counter where I could access it while in the kitchen and my family could reach it while sitting at the counter. The other big promise of HomeView is to act as a family hub, with everyone’s personal data easily accessible on a communal device in the home while staying separate for privacy. HomeView uses face and voice recognition to show up to six household members their calendars, messages, and calls — in theory, only to them when they’re in the home. If you have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone, it can also answer personal context requests. In practice, HomeView recognized me instantly, and I could swipe up from the home face to read my texts and access my calendar without any delay. But when it came to switching between profiles, it was too easy to access family members’ personal content. When I tested it with my teenage daughter, HomeView let me stay on her profile and scroll through her texts several times — even though it recognized me and popped up a prompt asking if I wanted to switch. [Image: [Image: While this didn’t happen every time, it happened often enough to be a problem, mostly when I used the device right after her. There’s a grace period where the device stays on your content even after you’ve moved away; and if I hopped onto the device within five seconds or so of my daughter leaving, I could sometimes scroll for up to 10 seconds before it checked again and locked me out. (This was purely for testing purposes and with her consent!) The other time we could reliably read each other’s content was when we were sitting side by side at the kitchen counter near the device. If my daughter was using it, walked away, and sat on the couch behind us, I could scroll through her messages for as long as I wanted because the camera still saw her in the room and didn’t switch to me, even though I was closer to it. [Image: The HomeView identifies who an incoming call is from and who it is for. Swiping out of Messages to a face and leaving the room was the most reliable way to protect our stuff — but it wasn’t foolproof. (Watch my video review for more on this.) I was impressed at how well HomeView switched between us on busy mornings. (Yes, my household does sometimes resemble that HomeView ad, minus the hole in the counter.) My daughter asked when her school project was due, then I jumped in to ask when to leave for the airport. HomeView answered each of us correctly, pulling from our respective calendars and texts — though we had to swivel the screen to face us, since it didn’t always recognize us by just voice. We could have used our phones, but HomeView’s large screen and louder speaker made hands-free use easier. HomeView was stricter with phone calls than text messages, ringing only when I was directly in front of it. When my phone rang while I was on the other side of the counter, HomeView stayed silent until I spun it around. This flow scuppers my hopes of using it as a family phone or putting it by my bed so I could banish my iPhone (and TikTok) to the living room at night. This is because it doesn’t show text notifications and won’t ring if it can’t see me, meaning I might miss a late-night call or text from my college-age son or teenage daughter. Siri AI lands in the home [Image: Siri AI appears in an interactive bubble at the top of the screen that changes depending on whether it’s listening, thinking, or processing. Tying all of these features together is Siri AI, which can answer general knowledge questions, control smart home devices, play music for you, and tap into personal context. I also didn’t have to repeat the wake word constantly; the Siri bubble animation on the screen clearly indicates when it’s still listening, so I could keep talking. Siri AI on the HomeView is an improvement over the older Siri on the HomePods, especially for controlling my home, and it’s mercifully much less verbose than its competitors. But it can be frustratingly slow to pull up personal context answers, sometimes makes mistakes, and regularly errors out. It is still in beta, so hopefully things will improve. [Image: Siri AI adds text explanations to tell you what stage it’s at. For smart home requests, Siri is very fast, since those run locally. It now responds to conversational requests like “dim the lights in here,” then “make it a bit dimmer,” making it easier to control devices. After it executes a voice command, it shows the accessory on the screen for additional control, which is handy. I could also create automations with voice, such as “Hey Siri, open the shades in my office at 8AM every morning” and chain commands like “turn on the lights in here and in the mudroom.” But these only work with one device type at a time, so I couldn’t control lights and the shades with one ask. I found Siri AI Personal Context handy in several instances, and it’s a feature that makes HomeView stand out from the competition — neither Alexa nor Google offers anything as deep. But here Siri can be slow, because it relies on pulling from your phone, and it struggles with anything taxing, like multiple requests in a row from different people. It frequently exclaims, “Uh oh, something’s wrong,” and gives up. Then there was the time Siri tried to send my husband in the wrong direction. He asked it about his weekend schedule, and it read out the events in his calendar at the Georgia Bushcraft Fall Gathering he was heading to. When he asked how long it would take to get there, it confidently told him one hour and 47 minutes. He then asked it to show him directions, and it couldn’t because it didn’t actually know the address. Siri had guessed the location based on something in the event that said “Dogwood Stage,” and had made up the travel time. The gathering was actually a five-hour drive away. The event’s address was in his email, but Siri didn’t connect those dots. [Image: Personal content on the HomeView includes Reminders, but these only appear when you’re at the device. I’d like the option for more communal apps for a household calendar, shopping list, or meal planning. When he prompted it to check his email, it found the correct address and calculated the drive time, but couldn’t pull up the route because there’s no Maps app on the HomeView. He asked it to send the route to his phone, and it said: “Done.” But all it sent him was a message with the drive time, no map attached. When he made the same request on his iPhone, it worked great. “It’s like your iPhone, but not as good” isn’t a great pitch here. Despite these hiccups, I did find myself using Siri AI on HomeView a lot more than I do on my phone, where touch is my first and easiest instinct. Beyond the basics [Image: [Image: Beyond the core functions of a smart display, HomeView starts to struggle. The built-in apps and widgets, which include Music, Calendar, Weather, Timers, Safari, and Intercom, work well. But if you want to use any other apps or widgets, they have to come from your phone, with some strange restrictions. They only work when your phone is at home, and only audio and video apps that support CarPlay and iPhone widgets that are compatible with the Mac show up. Because widgets point to apps that aren’t on the HomeView, they only work for glanceable info at best — tapping most of them gets you nowhere. This means the New York Times and Apple News apps that appeared on the device were just podcast feeds, not news apps, and the Ring widget just told me to use my iPhone. A few of the widgets I tested offered some on-screen info, and some could perform one or two pre-programmed actions — there’s potential here, but it’s frustrating on day one. The only video app that works on the HomeView is Apple TV, but the screen is letterboxed to essentially iPhone size, so I wouldn’t recommend anyone buy this for a video-watching experience. [Image: You can customize the app drawer and add more widgets. Safari is a workaround, and it’s not a terrible experience. I could browse websites by asking Siri to pull up The Verge or The New York Times in Safari, and I could log in to Netflix and YouTube using the pop-up keyboard. While I won’t be binge-watching the last season of Killing Eve on this, a Gordon Ramsay steak tutorial on YouTube while I cook, works fine but isn’t noticeably better than an iPhone. There’s also no Maps or Notes app — and I felt their absence. A share sheet and the ability to copy and paste from Safari are also MIA, so sharing a grocery list or texting a link meant going back to my phone. HomeView made me do that a lot, which underscores how many features of this product are an extension of my iPhone rather than a standalone device. How HomeView compares to the Echo Show and Nest Hub [Image: From left, the Google Nest Hub Max, the Apple HomeView, the Echo Show 11. I use and test all three major smart home platforms — Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple Home. After a week with HomeView and Siri AI, I rank Alexa Plus as the best smart home assistant, Gemini for Home as the smartest assistant, and HomeView as the best smart display hardware and personal assistant. Apple’s 7-inch square screen fits nicely into my home, and while it has similar dimensions to the Nest Hub, it has a smaller footprint. The Nest Hub Max, which launched in 2019, is showing its age and is significantly slower and laggier than HomeView. The newer Echo Shows 8 and 11 are closer to HomeView in capabilities, but not as snappy. The just-announced Show 16 has a new UI with similar features to HomeView, but Amazon’s penchant for sticking ads on its smart displays has rightly put off many users. The HomeView has no ads. [Image: Each smart display has its own AI assistant: Google has Gemini for Home, Apple has Siri AI, and Amazon has Alexa Plus. When it comes to the AI inside, Alexa Plus is the most capable in the smart home. It can run multi-device, multi-room commands in seconds, and you can create complex automations with voice alone. Gemini can also handle more complex multi-step requests and is better with natural language and inferring intent from vaguer statements, like “I’m cold,” which will have it turn up the thermostat. Where HomeView wins here is Personal Context. Google and Amazon offer similar profile switching, but neither is connected to your phone the way Siri AI is to your iPhone, so they have far less personal information to draw on. (Gemini for Home could certainly access much of it, but Google hasn’t gone there yet). Of course, this is also a drawback: you need an iPhone or iPad to have a profile on HomeView. However, guests or visitors can use the smart home controls, timers, weather, Safari, music, and Siri for general knowledge. Siri AI is also the only one of the three you don’t have to pay for to get the full voice assistant experience. Alexa Plus costs $20 a month or comes with Prime, and Google’s more advanced voice assistant, Gemini Live, is behind a paywall. Apple has said some Apple Intelligence features “are subject to daily usage limits,” with expanded access “available for a fee” in the future, but I didn’t run into any limits during my testing. However, Alexa Plus and Gemini Live are available on older smart speakers and displays; Siri is currently gated to the newest models. Alexa and Google also support many more smart home devices; I can’t control my Bosch coffee machine in Apple Home, and my Ring doorbell and Nest floodlight camera don’t natively work with HomeView. Which is a shame, as HomeView is the best smart display for cameras I’ve tested. Ring devices work almost as well on an Echo Show, but Nest cams are slow on a Nest Hub, and third-party cameras struggle on both. The catch is only a handful of brands work with HomeKit Secure Video — including Aqara, Eve, and some Anker Eufy and TP-Link Tapo models. Apple’s own cameras, made with LG, arrive next year. [Image: The HomeView makes a great photo frame. You select photos using your iPhone and can set them to rotate every few minutes. Apple is late, but pretty great HomeView is a very good first smart display from Apple: powerful enough to run my smart home but simple enough for anyone in it to use. If you’re an Apple household and want it for any of its core jobs, you’ll be pleased, and at $299 it’s very competitively priced. But it’s not the full-fledged family organizer some households might want; Skylight’s Calendar still owns that niche. Where it gets complicated is when it tries to be your iPhone. Siri AI and Personal Context bring something no other smart display currently offers. But potentially seeing each other’s texts will be a deal-breaker for some. Too many tasks send you back to your phone, and if Siri AI were a human personal assistant, I’d probably fire her for being too slow. This is all fixable: the option to turn off some personal features on the HomeView, a few more functional widgets and apps, and better options for displaying shared personal content like calendars could bring HomeView closer to the family computer I’d like it to be. Today, HomeView offers enough for its price to be a good choice for anyone with an iPhone or iPad who is intrigued by any of its core features — particularly the smart home. For households already deeply invested in the Apple ecosystem and Apple Home, the only real question is how many are you going to buy?

articles.title: Despite Putting the Spotlight on Tweek and Craig, South Park Delivers Another Miss in Season 29, Episode 5
articles.summary: Though South Park finally gives Tweek and Craig a long overdue episode, the execution leaves a lot to be desired in "We Be Clubbin'."
articles.body:
Full spoilers ahead for South Park Season 29, Episode 5!

I think we can officially give up on the notion of South Park Season 29 having any real sort of overarching narrative. Episode 5 comes and goes without even a nod to the recurring "GTA 6 is coming" gag, much less an attempt to build on the previous episodes in a significant way. The series has clearly swung back around to emphasizing standalone stories and trying to dig deeper into its ensemble cast. On paper, that's hardly the worst idea in the world, but for the third episode in a row, the execution leaves something to be desired.

I actually had pretty high hopes for "We Be Clubbin'." The Tweek/Craig relationship is one of the more low-key charming subplots in the series, and these two are long overdue for some time in the spotlight. This episode acknowledges as much when Cartman realizes to his horror that he and his classmates forgot the duo's anniversary. But for as much potential as a Heated Rivalry parody with Tweek and Craig in the lead roles had, this episode doesn't do enough to capitalize on that potential.

Once again, you have an episode that's guilty of beating the same horse over and over again till it's well past dead. This time the topic du jour is club sports and the predatory way they consume families' time, money, and sanity. In that sense, Tweek and his already anxiety-ridden family are perfect vessels through which to attack the institution. The problem, as is too often the case with South Park, is that the same jokes get repeated over and over again. We can only spend so long watching Tweek's parents wake up at 5am, rush around the state, whip out the old credit card, and deal with the other overachieving parents before the humor is just gone.

I mainly wish this episode had actually focused on Tweek and Craig more. What we do get from "We Be Clubbin'" in terms of relationship drama is pretty satisfying, but there's just not enough of that element. I would have liked the episode to fully commit to spoofing Heated Rivalry and get into the actual sports more (though I suppose that's the whole joke — there are no sports in club sports). It might also have helped if we saw more of Cartman and the gang sprinkled throughout the episode. But after the opening couple of scenes, those characters all but disappear from the episode.

Coming into Episode 5, I was also intensely curious to see how the show would reference the recent midterm elections. There's been a strong sense all season long that the writers really aren't that interested in focusing on topical political humor this season, and that's basically confirmed in the opening scene where Mr. Garrison reminds us it's no fun to punch down on "a fat loser." That scene is pretty entertaining in its brief acknowledgement of recent events, particularly as PC Principal drops the Power Christian shtick and returns to his old ways. I was also amused by the attempt to circle back around to the midterms at the end with Tweek's line, "You got swindled by a fat con man who played into your anxieties."

Episode 5 at least its head in the right place. It focuses on current events opnly as much as is strictly necessary before pivoting to a more standalone story geared around two underutilized characters. It just doesn't make the most of its premise or ultimately focus on said characters enough. And so Season 29's rough patch continues. Can the long-awaited arrival of GTA finally turn things around in the season finale? Let's hope so.

articles.title: Obsession 4K Collector’s Edition Is on Sale for $12.99
articles.summary: Obsession, the horror hit of 2026, is already on sale for just $12.99 at Amazon and Walmart.
articles.body:
When it landed in theaters earlier this year, Obsession was a major horror hit at the box office . Filmed for under $1 million and directed by 26-year-old YouTuber Curry Barker, it made many times its budget in its opening weekend alone. For good reason, if you ask me – it's an awesome movie. And right now Amazon , Walmart , and Gruv have the 4K collector’s edition on sale for just $12.99.

Obsession - Collector's Edition (4K UHD + Blu-ray + Digital)

The two retailers always price-match each other’s sale prices, so I’m not sure which one had it first. It may be Walmart, because Walmart is running an early Black Friday sale between now and November 15.

While the box calls this a "collector’s edition," it looks like a standard 4K release to me. It doesn’t come with any physical extras or anything. You just get the movie on 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and digital, plus some bonus features (detailed below). The digital copy of the film is Movies Anywhere compatible , so if you sign up for a free account and link your streaming services, you can watch it on pretty much anywhere.

As for the movie itself, it’s about an insecure guy who nurses a crush on his coworker, but she doesn’t like him as anything more than a friend. In a store he finds a “One Wish Willow” that looks like a novelty item, but it says it can make his wish come true. As a last-ditch effort to get the girl, he buys it and wishes she liked him. Reader, it’s not long before he has regrets. This is a dark movie that goes places , and I think we can leave it at that. Horror fans love it, and for good reason.

From IGN’s Obsession review : “Obsession should and will put Barker on the map as a horror filmmaker you need to watch. Thanks to fantastic turns by Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, you'll be addicted to this sour Valentine's Day counterprogramming. The film plays on familiar romance and monkey's paw tropes, turning a wish against the wishee, but Barker's execution takes things to the next level. In the film's simplicity lay the chance to go for broke, putting all efforts into the lengths Nikki is willing to go for her beloved. With that focus and Barker's fearlessness, Obsession becomes one hell of a maximalist ride.”

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: GTA’s Strangest Myths: A Full History
articles.summary: From bigfoot to the Mount Chilliad mystery, GTA has a long history of urban myths. Before GTA 6 adds more to the list, we investigate the series' most talked-about legends.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto has always run a second game beyond the boundaries of your controller, a scavenger hunt set in motion by a huge community of secret hunters determined to crack open the series and solve the meta mysteries within.

GTA is a lightning rod for urban legends and a magnet for myths, and hunters will stop at nothing to dig up the cryptids, creepypastas, and cut content that simply must be hidden somewhere in the vastness of each title.

What are the most famous rumors throughout the series’ history? Did any of them turn out to be true? And what does the future hold for sleuths and speculators in the age of leaks and datamining? These are GTA’s strangest myths.

Grand Theft Auto 3 launched after a last-minute, three-week delay out of sensitivity to the September 11th attacks. Not much was actually changed: only about 1% of the game by Rockstar’s own estimate, little things like police car livery and pedestrian barks.

But in the cauldron of conspiracism that was the early 2000s, we wondered what else we weren’t supposed to see. The gray city cast in hazy headlights felt lonely and liminal, with cars that spawned out of nowhere and a feeling that something clandestine was just around the corner.

Consider the Dodo, a Cessna with clipped wings that barely achieves liftoff. It’s not a massive leap to presume that the aircraft was grounded as part of the 9/11 cuts, or that it was originally part of a mission where it smashed into Donald Love’s towering HQ. Why else would Rockstar model a plane and implement flying controls just to hobble it?

But the Dodo was never intended to fly. A purported design document calls for a “wingless Cessna,” a compromise forced by the PS2’s data streaming pipeline. An airworthy Dodo would outrun the game’s ability to load itself.

There was no technical reason to cut Darkel. The lost character’s existence is well-supported. IGN’s early previews noted a prophet who “says weird things and asks you to do weird things,” and he appears in the design document as a creepy personification of the Rampage missions.

Why the omission? One theory is that his missions were too violent and taboo even for Rockstar. Think El Burro’s Ice Cream Truck mission but worse. Working for an anarcho-terrorist was a non-starter after 9/11, but Darkel was actually axed well before the attacks.

Not every character works out, especially when a floating skull icon could do their job with a lot less yappin’. Only fragments remain of Darkel in GTA 3: a name in the credits, an unused texture, and a circle of vagrants who haunt a Harwood tunnel.

The last of his followers, perhaps. Sometimes they have molotovs. No one knows exactly what they are up to, not even your friend’s uncle who works at Sony.

Schoolyards and study halls were the source of knowledge in the days before CCU numbers and open betas. The gaming press served enthusiasts who traded secrets in magazine letter pages and the message boards of hot new websites.

Mags would offer morsels of dirt in return, confirming and debunking rumors and sometimes creating them out of whole cloth, but monthly magazines could only move so fast.

The conversation was heading online, and gamers got there early. By 2001 the internet had grown into a massive incubator for myths and legends. For GTA fans, things were about to get hairy.

Liberty City, as realized in GTA 3, is a tiny place. It’s only about 3 square miles by most measurements, and the O.G. Vice City isn’t much bigger.

2004’s San Andreas is nearly five times the size of LC, an entire state with three whole cities and vast swaths of forest, desert, and farmland between them. There’s more room to explore and get lost in, with plenty of empty space for imagination to fill the gaps.

GTA: San Andreas pushes the aging game engine to its limit, producing lots of little moments of unreality in a game designed to simulate modern(ish) life. Ghost cars roll across the street with no one inside. A photographer flings himself off a cliff. Planes fall from the sky and scorch CJ’s face. All of these glitches in the Matrix can be explained by quirks of the code, but where’s the fun in that?

The anomalies and eerie draw distance fog give the lo-fi world a sense of simulacrum. There’s a haunting unknowability to San Andreas. Step off the beaten path and you’ll end up lost in the woods like a fairy tale. Here there must be monsters.

Rockstar excels at cheeky commentary on all things Americana, and it’s not a huge leap to presume that they must have included the country’s favorite cryptid somewhere in the San Andreas wilds. Some call him Sasquatch, the Skunk Ape, or Harry. Most know him as Bigfoot, the missing link of the Pacific Northwest. You’ve probably seen his beef jerky ads.

Bigfoot’s existence in San Andreas was surmised with staggering speed. Within days of San Andreas dropping, yarns were being spun online about mysterious UFOs and phone booths in the desert and a mythical creature roaming the countryside. But the “San Andreas Bigfoot Hunt” wouldn’t really pick up steam until the game came out a second time.

The “Hot Coffee” controversy, in which a scrapped sex minigame was discovered hidden on the disc, resulted in San Andreas being pulled from shelves and re-released without the offending material. There was definitive proof on the national news that Rockstar buried secrets within the game. Anything was possible now, even Bigfoot.

The pursuit of Bigfoot in San Andreas by the blossoming online myth-hunting community mirrors much of the real world search for the elusive beast. There are innocent mistakes, where fleeting glimpses of the mundane are misremembered as hulking monsters. A random pedestrian who mistakenly spawns in the woods can scare us enough to conjure a terrifying ape man in our minds. A creepy growl heard in the Back O’ Beyond woods after hours of searching could be the monster, even if it’s actually just C.J.'s stomach rumbling.

Much of the “evidence” for the real Bigfoot comes from shaky footage and blurry snapshots, and the same can be said for the San Andreas creature. In the pre-OBS age, when capturing video required dedicated hardware, sightings were shared as poorly-compressed files filmed straight from a smeary CRT. These vague images lack clarity but ooze spooky vibes, and the fuzziness plays a major role in maintaining an aura of forbidden mystery.

Rockstar itself addressed the rumor with co-founder Terry Donovan declaring in no uncertain terms that “there is no Bigfoot, just like in real life.” A doctored version of his quote spread through the community with quite the opposite effect thanks to the apocryphal addendum of “there is something in the woods.”

Bigfoot brings out a lot of fakers. Just ask the countless con artists throughout the decades who spent their hard-earned time on wooden footprints and fictional taxidermy. Even the most famous Bigfoot evidence of all, the Patterson-Gimlin film, was recently, nigh-definitively exposed as a hoax. The GTA myth hunter scene was equally rife with opportunists who shamelessly forged evidence for their pet theories, doubly so when the PC version of San Andreas arrived with the ability to mod in a Bigfoot, snap some screenshots, and stir the pot.

Speaking of the PC version, couldn’t a simple exploration of the data put the myth to bed once and for all? In theory, if Bigfoot existed in the files, modders would surely find remnants ala Darkel, but no one has ever produced an authentic model or texture. True believers aren’t moved by this lack of evidence.

Maybe he was on the original discs and was scrubbed after the Hot Coffee controversy, or removed in a later port. Patches provide the plausible deniability that’s essential for every enduring myth.

Rockstar was clearly aware of and amused by the Bigfoot craze. In 2010, Red Dead Redemption’s Undead Nightmare DLC directly confronts us with several Sasquatches, and killing one earns the achievement “Six Years in the Making,” reflecting the amount of time since the release of San Andreas.

The arrival of GTA 5 in 2013 heralded an entirely new crop of rumors for fans to obsess over, but the devs didn’t forget their first love. In the game, Franklin can meet a hunter who has been obsessively chasing Bigfoot for “eight years,” roughly corresponding to the gap between San Andreas and V. His quarry turns out to be a man in a costume, but later updates would allow the player to embody the actual monster as part of an extra convoluted golden peyote quest that seems straight out of schoolyard gossip.

The chase itself had become part of GTA lore, and the community it created would soon move on to a new monster.

The Sasquatch is a mostly rural, West Coast phenomenon, and doesn’t really suit the HD streets of Niko Bellic’s Liberty City in Grand Theft Auto 4 . A “Bigfoot of Bohan” allegedly haunts Welham Park, but GTA 4’s farcical take on the five boroughs deserved a cryptid that called it home. Enter Ratman.

New York is filled with critters. Pigeons, squirrels, the odd Eurasian eagle-owl. It’s not uncommon to take your garbage out and see an opossum’s eyes glowing back at you. But it’s the common brown rat that’s the city’s spirit animal, resilient, resourceful, and huge.

Living in NYC means dealing with the odd rodent jump-scare: a glimpse of movement out of the corner of your eye, a feeding frenzy around a discarded pizza box. Urban legends abound of giant rats lurking in the city’s sprawling tunnel system, mutant hybrids that walk and talk and scold their adopted children for inspiring Ninja Rap. Something’s got to be down there.

Like its real-world counterpart, GTA 4’s subway is impressively complex. Even though Niko can easily phone a cab and skip the trip, Rockstar implemented a true-to-life LTA transit system with four distinct lines and 26 stops. It’s fairly nonsensical by railfan standards, but there were plenty of places to hide.

The first Ratman forum threads were created within weeks of GTA 4’s release and met with skepticism at first, but the clues kept coming. Suspicious orange puddles appeared throughout the subway system. Players reported hearing odd squeaks when exploring the tunnels, with multiple posters claiming they heard a voice shout “I am the Ratman!”

These rumors were quickly dismissed, since cryptids don’t tend to introduce themselves. They do, however, excel at posing for blurry, inconclusive photo evidence. Before consoles slapped a Share button on every controller, myth hunters had to document their sightings the hard way. Our impressions of Ratman were filtered through Unregistered HyperCam 2 and the Moto RAZR’s VGA photo sensor. The results were so murky you didn’t need to Photoshop them, though plenty doubtless did.

The ambiguous imagery kept Ratman’s mystique intact and allowed us to speculate on his true nature. Is the orange liquid the blood or bile of a monstrous bipedal creature who feasts on the city’s unhoused population? Or could the Ratman simply be a ragged, disturbed human ala Darkel?

We would never find the answers, as Ratman was never conclusively found inside GTA 4 or any of its data. Still, the quest continued, even when it seemed like Rockstar was directly mocking it. An in-game article on the Liberty Tree website reports on urban myths causing widespread disturbances “in the minds of insane residents,” naming sasquatches, secret cities, and other infamous GTA mysteries. It wasn’t hard to get the impression that the developers were teasing us, but the community took it in stride and showed no signs of slowing down.

GTA myths are built on top of each other, hundreds coexisting at once across console generations. Whispers of aliens, of shady men in trenchcoats and ghosts of slain NPCs echo through decades. The GTA Myths wiki was founded in 2012 to catalogue this body of modern folklore and keep things honest. The massive database houses 1,500 pages of myths and rules them systematically with a verdict of proven, possible, unlikely, or false.

A few select rumors sit above this scrutiny, under the protection of the wiki’s Protected Heritage policy, the valhalla of unsolved GTA legends. Ratman and Bigfoot are there. So is Piggsy, the masked maniac from Rockstar’s Manhunt who fans swore was hiding in San Andreas. One entry is conspicuous in its absence from this pantheon, perhaps the biggest myth of all. The one that turned out to be true.

High above the foggy woods of Blaine County, overlooking the lonely Alamo Sea and towering over tiny towns of Grapeseed and Paleto Bay, is Mount Chiliad. It stands 800 meters above sea level, though a sign within the world claims it’s a staggering 2,700 meters, putting it in the same league as California’s Mount San Jacinto. Either way, it’s the tallest point in Grand Theft Auto 5 and it’s a lot of fun to climb.

There are many ways to reach the summit of Chiliad. You can hike the trails, drive up a dirt road, or pedal a bicycle until your thumb feels like it’s about to fall off. You can fly in by helicopter or drop in from a plane, but if you want a more leisurely ride to the peak and have 10 bucks to spare, a cable car will carry you up in comfort. Once they reached the station, players discovered the doorway to a mystery that would consume the GTA fandom for the next decade.

Scrawled on a wall beside two sealed doors is a mural: a crude diagram of Mount Chiliad crowned with a halo of lightning and topped by a beaming, all seeing eye. Inside the drawing, a network of lines connect boxes across the mountain, five of them marked with X’s. Along the bottom sit three strange symbols: a UFO, a cracking egg, and a humanoid figure with a shape on its back that sure looks like a jet pack.

The hunt was on. Mount Chiliad’s page on the highly influential GTA Myths wiki was created three days after GTA 5 launched in September of 2013. The subreddit r/ChiliadMystery, arguably the linchpin of the scene, formed four days later. Fresh off the Breaking Bad finale, communities across the internet turned their theorycrafting energy towards scouring the mountain for clues. Here’s what they found:

The X’s on the mural roughly correspond to points across the mountain where painted glyphs are hidden. The images depict the eye from the mural along with icons like the moon or a raincloud. One glyph is tucked beneath an observation platform. Above it, on the deck, before a breathtaking view, you’ll see a phrase: “Come back when your story is complete.

Rockstar wasn’t really being subtle. For the first time, it embraced rather than mocked the myth hunters in its midst, giving them more than a morsel to chew on. We didn’t have to engage in wild mass guessing over glitches and cut content and fuzzy memories anymore. GTA 5 provides an elementary ARG, with tangible clues and concrete goals and a story that evolves over time. What was the goal? What were we trying to find? The mural symbols seemed like promises.

Perhaps the egg was of extraterrestrial nature. There’s aliens abound in GTA 5, from DMT hallucinations to dudes in costumes. You can find one frozen in ice mere minutes into the tutorial. Conspiracy culture around little green men has long been a target of GTA, most notably in the original San Andreas’s Area 69. The mission saw CJ blasting out of a government compound with a jetpack, another object prioritized as a possible prize. That leaves the UFO.

It is indisputable that there are four unidentified flying objects in the game. Most appear at night, floating in the sky as high as the game engine will allow. Two of them resemble traditional hubcap flying saucers and are marked with FIB lettering, while the one at Fort Zancudo is matte black and seemingly manmade, like a reverse-engineered copy of the alien original. How does the military have access to this technology? It could be from the fourth spaceship found sunken on the ocean floor.

This is the answer to the Mount Chiliad mystery: After reaching 100% completion as the message prophesied, ascend Mount Chiliad during a rain storm, per the glyphs’ instructions. Stand on the lookout platform at 3:00 AM and behold: a UFO, quite similar to the other “Plan 9” style ships, though there are clues that this might be some sort of projection or hologram. Walk away and it vanishes, much like the dreams of many a myth hunter who had hoped for something more.

Many refused to believe that it ended with the UFO, convinced that the Chiliad was a red herring to disguise the real revelations still waiting to be discovered. They searched in vain for the jetpack, or poured their efforts into other myths like the ghostly woman who spawns atop Mount Gordo (true!) or the Goatman who lives beneath a bridge in Cape Catfish (not so much). The community wasn’t done with GTA 5, and neither was Rockstar.

About a year later, Rockstar re-released GTA V on PS4 and Xbox One, with a PC version the following spring. Upgrades included higher resolutions and first-person view, with sharper textures allowing for closer looks at clues. Subtle changes were introduced in the next-gen version as well: a creepy face found on the mountainside was replaced by a rooster, and a tiny tattoo appeared on Trevor’s hand, the same all-seeing eye symbol from the summit.

What did the developers mean by the alterations? Were we reading too much into it, or was Rockstar steering us toward the real answers? Does solving a mystery still count if the facts keep changing?

Detective fiction has a rule for this, called “playing fair:” the solution can’t hinge on something the reader has no way of knowing. You can’t slip DLC chapters into an Agatha Christie novel after the final page, but that’s how Rockstar has been running the hunt for years.

Grand Theft Auto Online turned the series into a living game, refreshed on a schedule with a constant stream of new content, from weapons and vehicles to game modes, heists, and eventually the holy grails we’ve devoted our lives to finding.

The Doomsday update in 2017 appears to be the final word on the Chiliad mystery, revealing a secret, high-tech facility inside of the mountain bearing the same iconography seen at the summit. The climactic heist sees you blasting out of Chiliad with the Thruster, the fully functional jetpack of our dreams. It costs about $2 million to keep it.

Other updates introduced ghost hunting, aliens, and trippy Sasquatch communion, and while there’s nothing wrong with giving the people what they want, there’s something deflating about handing out the payoffs to long-running myths in service of selling more Shark Cards. Our years of searching and deciphering ended with as much meaning as “be sure to drink your Ovaltine.”

The community is still around, but it’s never been the same since. Instead the energy has turned from finding secrets inside the games toward learning everything we can about them before release. The last few years of GTA rumors have revolved around high-profile leaks fed by the fevered frenzy for GTA 6. There are sure to be countless secrets and vast depths to discover within the most anticipated game of all time, but it’s going to feel different having peeked behind the forbidden curtain, knowing it can all change on a dime.

Games used to be a finished thing. You bought the disc, took it home, and, presuming there were no secret sex minigames inside, that was it. Everything there was to hide was already etched on DVD, secrets fixed in low-res amber exactly where we left them. The hunt will never end for Grand Theft Auto myths, because no one can patch out possibility.

Charlie "Moose" Lopresto graduated law school, passed the bar, and made a financially questionable decision to write about games and movies instead. Contributing to IGN since 2021, he collects solo board games and transforming robots.
