articles.title: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine Is a Twisted Western About the American Dream
articles.summary: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine is a new Western from Oni Press that asks, "What if, instead of selling your soul to the Devil, you found a way to sell other people’s souls?”
articles.body:
Between Out of Alcatraz and the recently launched Archie in Hell , Tyler Crook is easily one of the most important creators in the Oni Press talent pool. IGN can exclusively reveal Crook's next project at Oni, a harrowing Western called The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine.

Check out the slideshow gallery below for an early look at The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine #1:

The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine #1 Preview Gallery

The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine is a three-issue, prestige-format series that pairs Crook with artist Emily Schnall (Tales from Harrow County). The first issue features cover art by Crook, Schnall, Anand RK, and Noah Bailey.

Here's the official summary for the series:

In the harsh Western frontier of the mid-1800s, runaway teens Buck and Toby dream of finding their own destiny and wealth beyond the oppressive walls of the orphanage where they became brothers. With a small work crew, they set out for the Holy Ghost Mine, a silver stake deep in the hills of the Nevada Territory under the direction of the eager but inexperienced Henry Gaines. According to Henry, his father, Harlan, has developed a mysterious new technique that produces the highest quality silver—but when they reach the mining camp in the center of a great salt flat, they find empty barracks, an inactive mine shaft, and a frantic Harlan determined to send them quickly away... before it’s too late.

“THE FATHER, THE SON, AND THE HOLY GHOST MINE started with a simple question: What if, instead of selling your soul to the Devil, you found a way to sell other people’s souls?” said Crook in a statement. “From there the story evolved to become an exploration of friendship, family, and ambition. Everyone in this story is desperate to get their hands on something to make themselves feel complete. For some it’s wealth, for others it’s love, and some just want to find their way home. I’m excited for readers to enter this weird world which Emily Schnall is rendering with an expressive beauty that is going to knock everyone’s socks off.”

The Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost Mine #1 will be released on February 3. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

Do it, and you clean up the blood and bury the body before dawn. Refuse the voice, and it starts hunting you." And then I took a look at the moody, somewhat creepy trailer, complete with the built-in nostalgia of its PS1-era graphics, and I wanted to know more.
articles.body:
The pitch for Sankan, from solo developer Dany Rexton of YTKA Games, intrigued me. "You and up to two friends work the night shift at a mountain gas station in Japan, 1999," he told me via email. "The voice in your head names a customer you have to kill. Do it, and you clean up the blood and bury the body before dawn. Refuse the voice, and it starts hunting you." And then I took a look at the moody, somewhat creepy trailer, complete with the built-in nostalgia of its PS1-era graphics, and I wanted to know more.

Sankan is planned for release on PC in early 2027. And it's not just a single-player game. Up to three people can play together cooperatively. Everyone speaks in subtitles, as there is no dialogue. Rexton says there are "several" endings. Check out that trailer above, and take a look at the first screenshots in the gallery below.

"The people you met come back in later shifts. So does what you did," Rexton told me. Again, it's intriguing. If you'd like to follow along with development as the early 2027 release target nears, you can wishlist Sankan on Steam .

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Paper Tiger Review: James Gray’s Gritty Crime Drama Is a Tense, Tragic Character Study About Family and Ambition
articles.summary: Director James Gray returns to his crime drama roots with Paper Tiger, which features some of the strongest performances of Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson’s careers.
articles.body:
Paper Tiger opens in theaters November 13.

With Paper Tiger, director James Gray returns to a milieu familiar from his first three movies – Little Odessa, The Yards, and We Own the Night – and delivers one of his strongest films in years.

At the heart of this slow burn crime drama – set in Queens, New York in 1986 – are two brothers, family man Irwin Pearl (Miles Teller) and his older brother Gary (Adam Driver), a swaggering former cop who comes to his younger sibling with a business proposition. Utilizing his ties to City Hall, Gary wants to launch a consulting firm offering their services to recently arrived Russian immigrants who have started a clean-up firm for the polluted Gowanus Canal.

Gary, the wheeler-dealer, would get the Russians hooked up with his connections while straight-shooter Irwin, an engineer, would advise them on how to keep the operation up to code. With Gary being bled dry in a divorce and Irwin considering his eldest son’s looming college tuition, this business venture seems like a win-win for both brothers. Unfortunately, these Russians are actually a mob front. When Irwin sees them doing something he shouldn’t have witnessed, he, his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) and their two teenage boys are targeted.

Irwin and his family are not street-smart people. They’re a painfully ordinary, working-class family where the most dangerous thing they’ve seen is the revolver that ex-cop Gary keeps holstered to his ankle. Gary is essentially the serpent who enters their modest paradise, tempting Irwin to desire more than he already possesses. (The movie begins with a quote from Aeschylus: "Let there be wealth without tears; enough for the wise man who will ask no further.")

Gary is slick and has big ambitions, but he’s not a bad guy. As shady as he seems, it’s surprising to discover that, even when he was a cop, Gary possessed a moral compass. Adam Driver is, unsurprisingly, great here, revealing the complexities of a man who, like the titular paper tiger, may not be all that he blusters he is. Gary, who only allows his real vulnerabilities to be seen when alone, clearly loves his brother and extended family – even though he’s ultimately responsible for the danger they’re in. What he’s prepared to do about that puts him to the test.

Irwin is essentially impotent to protect his family, relying on Gary’s aid, who in turn thinks being a former cop will protect him. The Russians, though, aren’t La Cosa Nostra and Gary can’t cajole, bluff or bargain with these criminals the way he might have with the Gambinos once upon a time.

Ditching the bravado that marked his earlier roles, Miles Teller is a revelation as Irwin, a weak man trying to muster guts in a situation where he’s woefully out of his depth. He’s a schlub who makes dad jokes, not a guy who knows the ways of the street. Irwin here reminds me of Dustin Hoffman’s characters in Straw Dogs and Marathon Man, while Driver’s richly nuanced, “ain’t I a big man” performance is reminiscent of Gene Hackman or Robert Duvall’s work in their prime.

Meanwhile, Scarlett Johansson gives one of her best performances as Hester, a New York housewife with big curly hair who runs a tight household – and is keeping a big secret from her husband and beloved sons. Johansson’s reaction in a scene where Hester learns some shocking news is utterly authentic and heartbreaking.

The fear that upends the Pearl family’s life is so palpable because it’s utterly alien to their bland, ordinary world. They’re ill-equipped for the peril they’re in, as highlighted by an incredibly creepy home invasion sequence where what you hear is more unnerving than what you can see.

Shot on 35mm film by cinematographer Joaquin Baca-Asay, Paper Tiger looks like it really was made in the 1970s or ‘80s, with its graininess and imperfections adding to its period authenticity. Likewise, production designer Happy Massee and costume designer Amy Roth succeed in making Paper Tiger feel lived-in and genuine. You can practically smell the ash trays and Brut cologne.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Resonant Strings - Inanis and The Chord Memory Flower Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Resonant Strings is an optional collectible side quest in Phantom Blade Zero. Unlike most side quests, this is woven into the main story of the Crimson Forest
articles.body:
Resonant Strings is an optional collectible side quest in Phantom Blade Zero . Unlike most side quests, this is woven into the main story of the Crimson Forest and it is likely you will complete this without even trying to hunt down all the Memory Flowers.

This quest tells the story of The Chord and Inanis and begins when you pick up the first Memory Flower in the cave between Stone Hand Iron Fever and the Mirrorwood Long Pillar.

Find Inanis and The Chord's Memory Flowers

There are five additional Memory Flowers to collect as a part of this quest. They are all along the main path towards the final boss in the Crimson Forest and hard to miss.

On the main path, you'll find the next Memory Flower right next to the Burial Grounds Bell. Clear the enemies in the area in order to pick it up.

Follow the main path, past the Burial Grounds bell to find the next Memory Flower.

Progress onwards to the north, after you speak with Inanis and upon jumping down off the second set of cliffs after she clears the fog, you will find the next Memory Flower.

Continue onwards until you reach the riverbed in the Mirrorwood. Here you can find the next Memory Flower sat by the Mirrorwood Depths bell.

The next Memory Forest is just ahead in the first section of the Mirrorwood Forest maze. If you don't grab it in the moment, you won't be able to return.

Upon finding this flower, the quest will complete.

articles.body:
Nintendo has finally confirmed details for its 2026 Black Friday sale . Not only does it include a much-awaited $50 discount on Switch 2 consoles (effectively wiping out the September price hike), but it will also feature $20 off several Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 games.

Nintendo has confirmed a handful of games that will be included in the sale so far, but we'll have to wait to see the full list of offers when the sale kicks off on November 22.

So far, games confirmed to be included in the sale are Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby AirRiders, and Metroid Prime 4: Beyond for Switch 2, alongside Super Mario Galaxy 1+2 and Super Mario Party Jamboree for the original Switch.

Nintendo has stated that the aforementioned games will be available from $39.99 each, with a standard $20 discount applied across the board on the Switch exclusive games.

Not to confuse fans, but "starting at $39.99 each" may have some fans thinking that Donkey Kong Bananza will be down to $39.99, but since its MSRP is still $69.99 in the US, we're expecting its price to be $49.99. That should also apply for Kirby AirRiders and Metroid Prime 4: Beyond.

Nintendo has also confirmed that Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, GameStop, and the official Nintendo Store will carry these offers during the Black Friday sales at each respective retailer.

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV

Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?

It's not necessary to wait for what I like to call Black Friday proper if you only after the games in the official Nintendo sale. While most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before the big day.

Nintendo is following this trend with the deals starting on November 22, five days before the official sale day that no retailer ever sticks to these days. But., having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits, it usually sticks for the rest of the sale.

That means the prices you see on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to the end of November, and while not yet confirmed, likely December as well. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there will be no need to wait any longer once the sale starts.

These offers are reliable and worthwhile. But, you should still keep an eye out for more deals on other third-party games in the coming days as well, alongside plenty more from the Nintendo exclusive catalog.

articles.title: How to Get Void Pearls - Steal An Egg [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Void Pearls are a special resource that you can unlock while playing Steal an Egg. They are available alongside the Alien Biome. You'll need to reach this
articles.body:
Void Pearls are a special resource that you can unlock while playing Steal an Egg . They are available alongside the Alien Biome . You'll need to reach this area and be fast enough to run if you want to acquire them. In this guide, we're going to be sharing with you everything you need to know about how to get Void Pearls while playing Steal an Egg.

You can get Void Pearls as milestone rewards for catching fish. Make your way to the Alien Planet biome, behind the Enchanted Forest, and speak with the Alien Ferryman. The Alien Ferryman will be able to offer to take you to a different location, where you have a private lagoon to catch fish. If it's your first time meeting the Alien Ferryman, they give you a fishing rod and ask you to catch 20 fish, and they reward you with the location. You'll be able to do so from the waterfall location in the Alien Planet biome.

Alternatively, you can fish from the dock of the Alien Planet biome. Both are viable options for you to catch fish, so long as you have a fishing rod. The one from the Halloween Event is also an option, at least at first.

Every time you go to catch a fish, when you reel it in, there's a chance you can acquire a small amount of Void Pearls. The amount varies based on the type of fishing rod you're using. Better rods yield more Void Pearls. Though they're still small amounts, especially when you need 1,750 Void Pearls to unlock one Dark Matter mutation to place on your eggs. The chance to get Void Pearls is alongside the other rewards you can reel in, such as eggs, relics, or mutations.

Additionally, there are Fishing Milestones. As you catch fish in the Alien world, the Fishing Milestones page meter gradually goes up based on how many points you get. Every successfully caught fish counts as one point. On the milestone page, you can review how many you need for Void Pearls.

When you're ready to redeem those Void Pearls, speak with the Alien Ferryman. There's an option to trade your Void Pearls for you to receive Dark Matter mutations to put on your eggs.

articles.title: Palworld Developer Pocketpair Gives Employees 5 Days Off to Play GTA 6
articles.summary: Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6.
articles.body:
Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6 .

“All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches,” the company said in a tweet . The company also shared a letter it presumably sent out internally to workers at the studio.

“To all employees,” the letter started. “On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin.

“At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday.

The holiday period starts on GTA 6 launch date, November 19, and ends on November 23. “During this period, employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to take a business trip to Vice City,” the letter said.

“We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.”

All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches. Please see the attached notice for details. — Palworld (@Palworld_EN) November 12, 2026

All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches. Please see the attached notice for details.

Pocketpair boss Takuro Mizobe tweeted to confirm he'll be making the most of the special holiday, saying: "Of course, I’ll be taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too!"

Pocketpair isn’t the only company talking about GTA 6’s launch. The developer behind Wardogs encouraged its players to “go play GTA 6” and come back to the game after its next big update. Hardware company Logitech also announced that it will be giving employees time off for GTA 6 . According to a new report, GTA 6 has caused a 17% spike in people requesting time off work , so it’s probably for the best.

Not long now! GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. articles.title: How to Get Nebuloth Kraken - Steal An Egg [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Nebuloth Kraken is a divine fish that you can catch while playing Steal an Egg. Not only do you have a small chance to catch this creature, but you'll
articles.body:
The Nebuloth Kraken is a divine fish that you can catch while playing Steal an Egg . Not only do you have a small chance to catch this creature, but you'll be directly competing against every other player across all of the servers. It appears for a short time, and you have to act quickly. In this guide, we'll be covering everything you need to know about how to get the Nebuloth Kraken while playing Steal an Egg.

Where to Catch a Nebuloth Kraken in Steal an Egg

You need to unlock the Alien Lagoon area by speaking with the Alien Ferryman. You can find them in the Alien Biome, behind the Enchanted Forest. Speak with the Alien Ferryman and complete their first quest, which is to catch 20 fish.

However, gaining access to the Lagoon is not the only thing you need to wait for, as there's a specific time when you can catch the Nebuloth Kraken. It only appears during a Cosmic Eclipse event. These events happen every 30 minutes, and these occur every :55 and :25 on the hour. You need to make sure you're already in the Lagoon leading up to this event.

While you're in the Lagoon, rather than being sent back to your base, you can remain in the Lagoon to catch fish. From there, wait until the Cosmic Event begins and a notification goes out to all servers. Although the event lasts for five minutes, you likely only have seconds to try to catch your Neuloth Kraken.

At the top of your screen, you'll see how many Nebuloth Krakens are available. There are only 750 across all servers. After 750 players from the entire game catch at least one Neuloth Kraken, they disappear, and you'll need to wait another half-hour for the Cosmic Eclipse event to appear again, and repeat the process. It all comes down to luck when attempting to catch one of these creatures, unfortunately. While you're waiting, you can spend time attempting to loot more Void Pearls .

articles.title: GTA 4’s Three Leaf Clover Heist Showed How Not to Rob a Bank – Art of the Level
articles.summary: This is how Michael Mann’s Heat inspired GTA 4’s legendary Three Leaf Clover mission, shaping Rockstar’s realistic sound design and the future of videogame heists.
articles.body:
Ask a dozen average punters what the best mission in GTA 5 is, and you’ll get several dozen answers. Ask the same box of eggs about Grand Theft Auto 4 and a consensus will emerge: it's Three Leaf Clover . A bickering bank-heist that starts on the border of outright slapstick but quickly turns into a masterclass of escalating tension, where the streets of Liberty City become a Pac-Man maze of hot flying lead in yet another glorious Grand Theft Homage to the works of filmmaker Michael Mann. It’s the crowning achievement of an otherwise very divisive game.

GTA 4 remains the most curious beast in Rockstar’s blockbuster menagerie: a brand new start in an era of unprecedented sophistication and visual fidelity, with the ever-capable hardware of the time leveraged into depicting the cold forever-autumn of Liberty City: a suitable backdrop for the grubby, boldly bleak tale of a man on the run from his past, a story chiefly about disillusionment, of treacheries within and without. A far cry from the endless summers of Vice City and San Andreas. If California knows how to party, New York City knows how to freeze your bollocks off on a park bench.

GTA 4 was in the same breath a huge step forward for Rockstar’s world-building and storytelling chops, while also being a deliberate back-to-basics reset for their flagship series. Structurally, it’s a lot closer to the original GTA and GTA 3 than its immediate predecessor, San Andreas , and it’s even less sophisticated than Vice City in key areas. GTA 4 has no real estate sub-game. Niko cannot gain weight by stuffing his face, or get jacked by lifting stuff. GTA 4’s missions tend to be short, sharp, shooty-bang vignettes where the player only has to work against the game’s chief objects of friction: angry NPCs with guns, and the unforgiving driving model that makes your average canalboat-sized American sedan handle like a bouncy castle on swampland.

In short, it’s brilliant. But it does leave us with only one real answer when it comes to its best or most iconic mission, and that’s when you tag along with the Irish mob for a hastily undertaken bank heist in Chinatown.

Though Three Leaf Clover is credited by Rockstar itself for inspiring the intricately designed heists of GTA 5 and GTA Online — as well as the lauded three-protagonist mechanic allowing players to switch between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor at key moments — Three Leaf Clover itself barely hints at such complexities. If anything, it’s the complete antithesis of a GTA 5 heist: there’s no planning involved, save for the almost arbitrary requirement to go buy a suit and tie and a hasty en-route briefing from Patrick McCreary.

Unsurprisingly given the lack of prep, things go wrong from the off. While Patrick and Derrick are arguing about how to treat the hostages, one of them, an idiotic NRA member, decides to be today's "good guy with a gun". Michael Keane, not Batman’s butler, cops it when Eugene Reaper unconceals his carry. For the final time, as it turns out, when Patrick and Derrick shoot him to death in revenge. Luis Lopez, the tertiary protagonist of the GTA 4 saga and star of the Ballad of Gay Tony DLC, keeps his head down sensibly, although the player can choose to kill him if they enjoy messing with the space-time continuum.

The vault is blown with probably too much C4, a cool million dollars gets shoved into duffel bags, and all hell breaks loose on the streets: the bank is descended upon by scores of LCPD. Hundreds of cops and dozens of patrol cars block every escape route, turning the streets into killing corridors. Cover is scarce and flimsy: Niko can peek around corners, duck behind bins, or use parked cars as makeshift shield walls. Unfortunately, in hails of gunfire, cars are liable to explode, due to this being an era when people could afford to put gas in them.

The cavernous tenements and skyscrapers echo with barrages of bullets. Footsteps bounce around the walls as the crew dives into a subway station in a desperate attempt to get out of the open. The player somehow hears all this over the thumping of their own heart. If Niko dies, it’s back to Patrick’s mum’s house for a restart. If either of your companions die, it’s over. Kill too many civilians? Also a fail state. Lose the money? Fail. Car blows up? Fail. Abandon your crew? Fail. There are no mid-mission checkpoints: Three Leaf Clover is a mission that requires as much luck as skill to clear. It’s not an especially hard mission, but it’s easy to have a bad time with it through no fault of your own. Conversely, it’s perfectly possible to stumble through it with dumb luck. You need good fortune to make a fortune. As with all GTA missions, the game’s open world systems can work with or against you.

And this is a huge part of why it’s so tense. If you’ve been unlucky in your first attempt, the stakes get higher with every subsequent run: this is a crucial story mission that unlocks the last third of the entire map. But aside from the consequences of failure, Three Leaf Clover’s sheer lack of bells and whistles gives the whole experience an air of deadly realism that cuts through GTA’s baseline silliness by stripping it back to its most basic elements. Shooting. Running. Driving. Cops and robbers. Borrowing heavily once again from the works of filmmaker Michael Mann, most obviously 1995’s Heat, Three Leaf Clover refuses the temptation to underscore its action with the appropriate musical accompaniment, instead painting a symphony of death with strictly diegetic audio. No needle drops. No radios to bark crisply with the dialogue of your colleagues, no matter how far away they are. The sound is raw, real, unsweetened. Or, at least, it’s painstakingly designed to seem that way, and so successfully that you’re liable to forget that these are all sounds being triggered by clever scripting and a sophisticated real-time engine.

It’s this approach to sound design that really hammers home how much the people behind GTA are in love with Mann’s filmography, to the point where Grand Theft Auto is probably the most significant cultural force keeping the relevance of Miami Vice alive. Vice City and the upcoming GTA 6 are obviously massively indebted to what was one of the greatest TV shows of the 1980s, a rare example of one that still absolutely holds up today. The juxtaposition of pina coladas, speedboats, and sharp suits against a seedy criminal drug trade fuelling gang violence and urban decline certainly must have appealed to the Houser brothers and many of their collaborators, given how much of their stock in trade is based on those exact vibes. And it’s not hard to imagine why even the tainted glamour of a crime-ridden Miami would seem like paradise to kids growing up in 1980s Britain, purely by virtue of the fact that everything didn’t look like it was covered in a thin film of shit.

Miami Vice is just one side of the coin when it comes to Michael Mann’s influence on GTA: much is made of how Three Leaf Clover is directly inspired by the brilliant bank heist in Heat, right down to the outfits, which explains why Patrick McCreary is so insistent on Niko looking the part before the mission can even start. Three Leaf Clover plays out markedly differently to the Heat heist, with the inherent claustrophobia of Liberty City’s labyrinthine streets and alleys feeling a lot less exposed than the wide thoroughfares of downtown LA. But anyone who watches Heat for the first time will be struck by how minimalist the score is for such a high-stakes action thriller.

Where there is non-diegetic music, it’s often as simple and bare as a single note or drone denoting the mood: this maximises the impact of any gunshot that crackles over the mix, cutting the music entirely like a drum solo. And it’s highly important that this impact is not artificial: the gunshot must be heard and felt by those on screen, rather than dubbed over in post. To that end, Michael Mann uses on-location audio wherever possible, infamously using weapons loaded with full-charge blanks in his action scenes in order to get that real, terrifying sound without relying on post-production editing. As I’m writing this, the news has just broken that he recently shot himself in the foot at a shooting range, quite possibly having now invented Method Directing.

But even outside of action scenes, quiet conversations are given visceral impact by this minimalist technique: the iconic face-to-face meeting between Al Pacino and Robert De Niro is soundtracked not by trebly strings or terse pizzicato, but by the ambient din of a busy diner dialled up to oppressive levels. Again, this audio is captured on set, as the actors say it, with all that racket going on around them. Most other filmmakers, or cowards, would have a quiet set or ADR this in post. But that’s why most films sound…otherworldly. Not quite a product of the real world. Because they’re built out of duct tape and bullshit. Michael Mann’s films are no different, but I would argue that the techniques we’ve been talking about perhaps remove one layer of artifice between the viewer and the world they’re glimpsing on screen. You feel like you’re in that Collateral cab. You’re drilling that safe alongside James Caan in Thief. You can practically smell the perversion wafting from Manhunter’s Dollarhyde. All that fun stuff.

Grand Theft Auto’s designers are devotees of this naturalistic approach, of working with the fundamental elements of the audiovisual toolkit in order to achieve impact. Most of GTA’s audio is diegetic by design, even its scant few needledrops are usually at least conceptually delivered via the in-game radio. But Rockstar has to work backwards to achieve this kind of environmental naturalism: while filmmakers like Michael Mann, David Fincher, and David Lean could work magic out of the basic building blocks of light and sound to achieve gloriously dramatic results, cinematic minimalism or realism takes a whole lot of fakery to achieve in a real-time game engine.

The heat-haze of San Andreas, the soft, filmic quality of Red Dead 2 that evokes classic westerns, the smartphone shot Snapmatic reels of GTA 6: none of these styles are a happy consequences of pointing and shooting, but the planned and hard-won result of artisan engineers with extraordinary talent and a functionally infinite budget to work with.

In the end, Three Leaf Clover is a simple mission with simple objectives that is elevated by style, and the uncompromising boldness of its designers. You can make the argument that it is functionally little more than a high-fidelity rendition of Space Invaders if you want to, but that would be missing the point. It is, like the rest of GTA, all about making you give a shit. The humour, the frustration, the tension, the payoff: you are invested in Niko’s story because it feels real. And nothing exemplifies the wizardry and parlour tricks it takes to achieve that more than Three Leaf Clover, an ode to the detached, hyper-real style of Michael Mann at his best. It’s style and substance colliding to create a masterpiece.

In order to build Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption into the ambitious, intricately designed, systems-driven worlds of intrigue that they would eventually become in the HD era, Rockstar had to dial back to the bare essentials. And in order to get back to basics, GTA 4 had to be a powerhouse of audiovisual engineering. With its pioneering work on getting the Euphoria physics engine to play ball in a vast real-time simulated environment, its rich and detailed simulation of cinematic fundamentals that is so pristine that it looks easy, and excellent character work and writing that gave rise to the video game as HBO box set paradigm that we now take for granted as what video games are just like now.

Tl;dr: yeah it's really good, it's like that bit in Heat .

Jim Trinca is a Video Producer at IGN, and when he isn't fawning over Assassin's Creed, he can be found watching Star Trek and playing manservant to a horrid little cat. Follow him on @jimtrinca.bsky.social , and check out The Trinca Perspective playlist over on IGN's YouTube channel!

articles.title: Tech layoffs tracker 2026: All the job losses across Disney, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Meta and more
articles.summary: There are only a couple of months left of the year and there have been over 200,000 layoffs across the tech industry. Here are the details.
articles.body:
We've been inundated with tech layoffs throughout the whole of 2026 — and there's likely more to come. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft's round of layoffs in July affected 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Following that, companies like Samsung, Zillow and even TikTok joined the club.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." In addition, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 200,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Disney is reportedly planning to lay off thousands in an effort to cut annual costs by 20%. Layoffs have not been confirmed yet, but we'll update this story if and when they are. According to people familiar with the matter, the cost reductions could come from layoffs in addition to expense reductions.

Squarespace, the website-building company, is laying off 19% of its workforce, which amounts to about 300 people. "The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth," Jeff Seedman, a representative from Squarespace, told TechCrunch. Squarespace's industry has been disrupted by AI, as "vibe-coding" website builders have become more popular.

Design software company Canva's recent layoffs will impact 22% of its staff, or just over 1,200 employees. According to reports , the company is reorganizing its business and merging its product, growth and platform teams. Canva is also looking to reduce "subspecialisation," which could result in remaining employees taking on more responsibilities.

Fintech company Block started its second round of layoffs recently, after cutting more than 4,000 jobs earlier this year. According to reports , the Jack Dorsey-led company hasn't disclosed how many jobs were affected this time around, but reportedly teams at Cash App and Square (both owned by Block) were affected.

Amazon reportedly laid off "fewer than 1,000 white-collar workers" in its stores division. That's the part of the company that oversees the tech giant's e-commerce website. Employees in the U.S., India and the United Kingdom were reportedly affected.

In an additional incident, Amazon laid off about 250 employees in its devices and services unit, according to a Reuters report . This comes after a number of new product announcements, including new Kindles and Echo devices . According to the report, the cuts mostly affect those in software development.

The cloud storage company Dropbox is laying off about 9% of its workforce, which accounts for roughly 200 employees. The job cuts primarily affect workers on the engineering, product, design, and G&A teams. "Today, we're making difficult choices about where we invest and how we organize Dropbox to achieve the product and growth priorities that will matter most for our long-term strategy," Dropbox co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi said in an email to staff. Alkarmi also announced that, alongside the layoffs, chief technology officer Ali Dasdan will step down.

While not officially new layoffs just yet, reports claim Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This is in an effort to further reduce costs in the wake of increased AI usage. According to the reports, Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance divisions will be participating in the offer. Microsoft already laid off thousands of workers so far in 2026.

EBay will reportedly cut 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations. The latest job cuts come after a previous round of layoffs back in February, which affected about 800 positions. "As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in a statement.

Vide game publisher EA will eliminate 400 jobs , or about 3% of its workforce. This includes shutting down BioWare , the development studio behind the Mass Effect games. The next Mass Effect title will be cancelled as a result of the layoffs. These job cuts come after EA told investors earlier this year that it would reduce research and development costs as part of a plan to save upwards of $700 million.

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Netflix will lay off about 1,000 people, which accounts for about 6% of its global workforce. The report says the bulk of the layoffs will affect Netflix's "product, tech, legal and human-resources teams." This latest round of layoffs is the biggest for the company since 2022, and it comes in the wake of Netflix struggling to increase customer engagement and overall growth.

A "large part" of the Airtable team was laid off on October 12. Federico Simionato, Airtable owner Bending Spoons' product leader, said on X that the layoffs were not due to the workers' abilities but rather the company's "deep belief that small teams ship more and better." The exact number of employees affected by the layoffs wasn't disclosed.

Workday will be laying off around 140 employees from the Bay Area, as part of an effort to trim its tech team. The cuts come as part of a broader plan to cut the company's global workforce by 2.5%.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: As Xbox Turns 25, CEO Asha Sharma Says 'A Single Person Will Soon Be Able to Wield Capabilities That Once Required Entire Nations'
articles.summary: Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."
articles.body:
Xbox chief Asha Sharma has discussed her vision of the video games industry's next 25 years, and suggested its future lies in small teams or individuals able to "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

Sharma's essay, posted today on X/Twitter ahead of Xbox's quarter century anniversary this weekend, seems to take pains not to explicitly reference A.I. by name. But in a section looking ahead to the future of the Xbox brand and video games in general, the huge role that Sharma apparently believes A.I. will play is made pretty clear.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," Sharma wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable trade-off of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break," Sharma continued. "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

It's hard to imagine that this version of the future could be possible without the heavy use of A.I. tools in game development — a topic that is still highly controversial among video game fans, even as it becomes all the more ubiquitous behind the scenes.

For industry watchers, though, and also for Xbox employees, Sharma's message also points to something else: a vision of game creation that's far leaner than now in terms of financial cost and human investment. After a another year of brutal layoffs across the video games industry and within Xbox in particular , this concept will likely do little to reassure anyone currently at the games development coalface.

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays," Sharma concluded. "Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

Sharma oversaw 1,600 job losses within Xbox back in July of this year, and laid out a plan for a further 1,600 employees to be shed over the rest of this year. This led to the company shedding several game developers — small teams — like Double Fine and Ninja Theory and reorganizing beloved studios like id Software this fall.

The 25th anniversary of Xbox is on Sunday, 15 November.

articles.title: Cosmic Eclipse Event - Steal An Egg [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Cosmic Eclipse event in Steal an Egg is an important bihourly event that you can participate in to earn a special reward. However, it all comes down to
articles.body:
The Cosmic Eclipse event in Steal an Egg is an important bihourly event that you can participate in to earn a special reward. However, it all comes down to whether you can get lucky or not to earn this reward. In this guide, we'll be covering everything you need to know about the Cosmic Eclipse event while playing Steal an Egg.

How the Cosmic Eclipse Event Works in Steal an Egg

The Cosmic Eclipse event in Steal an Egg is an event that happens every 30 minutes. When it occurs, you'll have a short amount of time to make your way to the Alien Lagoon. You can unlock this location by speaking with the Alien Ferryman in the Alien Planet biome , next to the Enchanted Forest.

The main appeal of this event is an attempt to get the elusive Nebuloth Kraken . It's a divine fishing catch that exclusively appears during this event. There are only ever 750 of them available across all servers. When 750 players catch them (typically on their first try), they disappear, and you have to wait the full 30 minutes for another chance to catch one. These events occur every :55 and :25 of an hour, giving you two attempts every hour to try and catch one for yourself.

You'll always receive a notification when the Cosmic Event goes live, but you can be in the Alien Lagoon when this happens. You can make your way over here during the time leading up to the event. This way, when the Cosmic Eclipse happens, you can attempt to catch the Nebuloth Kraken and be among the first 750 people to try fishing for one. It all comes down to luck, unfortunately.

To increase your chances of acquiring one, stick around at the Alien Lagoon to attempt to catch more, and you'll likely unlock more Void Pearls and acquire better fishing rods from your Fishing Milestone rewards.

articles.title: Disney Marking Star Wars 50th Anniversary With Fresh A New Hope Making Of Documentary
articles.summary: Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope.
articles.body:
Disney has announced its plans for the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, which will include a fresh documentary detailing the making of A New Hope .

George Lucas' original Star Wars film debuted back in 1977, kicking off what would become one of the world's most popular and lucrative film and TV franchises. Half a century on, Disney+ will debut "The Hero Awakens," a brand-new documentary featuring rare archival footage from A New Hope's production, helmed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker R.J. Cutler.

The Hero Awakens will drop via Disney+ on Star Wars' annual May 4th celebration, following the theatrical re-release of Star Wars on February 19. This will be the rarely-seen original 1977 version of the movie — back when Jabba the Hutt was not a CGI slug and Greedo actually shot first.

In terms of what's actually new for the Star Wars franchise next year, Ahsoka Season 2 will drop via Disney+ on January 20, while Star Wars: Starfighter will land in theaters on May 28.

Both are anticipated, though will arrive at a time of great uncertainty for the Star Wars franchise in general, following the decidedly mixed response to Disney's sequel trilogy, several short-lived Disney+ TV projects, and a lengthy slate of movie projects cancelled or stuck in development hell. Not even a big screen outing for The Mandalorian and Grogu this year could turn things around, as the movie set a rather disappointing record for the franchise's lowest live-action theatrical gross.

Looking further ahead, a press release for Star Wars' 50th anniversary states that 2027 will bring a year of "new project announcements, anniversary merchandise, dedicated fan events, archival releases, and reimagined Disney Parks and Cruiseline offerings." Exactly what these project announcements are remains to be seen, though it seems likely we'll get a sense of the franchise's future before next year is out.

How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend

With Ahsoka and Starfighter the only remaining live-action Star Wars TV and movie projects publicly announced, the time has certainly come for Lucasfilm's newly-installed co-president Dave Filoni to map out what's next. Reports suggest that of everything Lucasfilm has previously announced, the new movie/trilogy written by Dark Phoenix's Simon Kinberg is the one currently moving forward .
